title: Casado (Costa Rican rice, beans, plantain and chicken plate)

ingredients.name: cooked black beans, with their liquid
ripe plantains, sliced on the diagonal

steps: Cook the rice with 600 ml of salted water and a spoonful of oil, covered, for about 15 minutes until the water is absorbed, then rest it for 10 minutes.
Sweat half the onion and one garlic clove in a little oil, add the beans with their liquid and simmer for 10 minutes, mashing a few against the pan, until saucy. Season with salt and cilantro.
Season the chicken with salt, pepper, crushed garlic and lime juice, and sear it in a hot pan for 5 to 6 minutes per side until cooked through.
Fry the plantain slices in 1 cm of hot oil for 2 minutes per side until deeply golden and caramelised at the edges, then drain.
Toss the cabbage and tomato with lime juice, salt and the remaining onion for a simple fresh salad.
Arrange rice, beans, chicken, plantains and salad on each plate with a warm tortilla at the side.

title: Chicharrones (Costa Rican crisp fried pork)

ingredients.name: pork belly, skin on, cut in 3 cm pieces

steps: Put the pork, garlic, lime juice, water and salt in a wide heavy pan so the pieces sit in one layer.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat and let the water evaporate gradually, about 30 minutes, turning the pork occasionally.

When the water is gone the fat will begin to render. Keep cooking over medium heat, turning the pieces, for another 20 to 25 minutes until they fry in their own fat and become deep golden and crisp outside.
Lift the chicharrones onto paper towels to drain and sprinkle with a pinch of salt.
Serve hot with lime wedges, tortillas, yuca or beans.

title: Churchill (Costa Rican shaved ice dessert with milk and syrup)

ingredients.name: red fruit or cola-flavoured syrup (grenadine works)

steps: Chill four tall glasses or bowls in the freezer for 15 minutes.
Pile crushed ice about two-thirds of the way up each glass, pressing it down lightly.
Pour syrup over the ice so it soaks through, using 1 tablespoon per serving.
Sprinkle 1 tablespoon of powdered milk over each and drizzle the condensed milk on top.
Add a scoop of vanilla ice cream to each, then more syrup if you like, and a cherry.
Serve immediately with a long spoon and eat before the ice melts.

title: Patacones (Costa Rican twice-fried green plantain with black bean dip)
steps: Cut the ends off the plantains, score the peel lengthwise and pry it off, then slice the flesh into rounds about 3 cm thick.
Heat 2 cm of oil to medium heat and fry the rounds for 2 to 3 minutes per side until pale golden and softened, then lift out onto paper towels.
While still warm, press each round between two pieces of parchment or with the bottom of a flat glass until about 5 mm thick.
Raise the heat and fry the flattened rounds again for 2 minutes per side until crisp and golden, then drain and sprinkle with salt immediately.
For the dip, blend or mash the black beans with the garlic, cumin, onion, cilantro and lime juice with a splash of bean liquid until thick and spreadable, and season with salt.
Serve the patacones hot with the bean dip.

title: Picadillo de ayote (Costa Rican squash and corn hash)

ingredients.name: tender young squash (ayote tierno), or zucchini/courgette, diced

steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan and cook the onion and bell pepper over medium heat for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes until saucy.
Stir in the diced squash and corn with a pinch of salt.
Cover and cook over low heat for about 12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the squash is tender but still holds its shape. Add a splash of water if it begins to stick.
Stir in the cilantro, adjust the salt and pepper and serve with rice, beans or tortillas.

title: Picadillo de papa (Costa Rican diced potato hash)

ingredients.name: waxy potatoes, peeled and cut in small cubes

steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan and sauté the onion and bell pepper for 4 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and cumin and stir for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes until they break down.
Tip in the potatoes and stir to coat them with the vegetables.
Pour in the stock, cover and cook over medium-low heat for 15 to 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed.
Uncover and cook for a few more minutes if it is too wet, and fold in the cilantro and seasoning.
Serve with rice, beans and tortillas, or as a filling in tortillas.

title: Picadillo de plátano verde (Costa Rican green plantain hash with beef)
steps: Peel the plantains by scoring the skin lengthwise and prying it off, then boil them in salted water for about 15 minutes until tender, and cut into small cubes once they are cool enough to handle.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and brown the beef over high heat for 5 minutes, breaking it up well.
Add the onion, bell pepper and garlic and cook for 4 minutes until soft, then stir in the cumin and tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the plantain cubes and a splash of water, folding gently so the pieces keep their shape.
Cook for another 5 to 8 minutes until everything is well combined and slightly browned at the edges, then stir in the cilantro and season to taste.
Serve with rice and beans or tucked into warm tortillas.

title: Tamal navideño (Costa Rican Christmas pork tamale)

ingredients.name: squares of banana leaf, softened over a flame

steps: Simmer the pork in salted water with the onion, garlic and cilantro for about 1 hour until tender, then slice or shred it and keep 700 ml of the broth.
Beat the lard until fluffy, add the masa harina and gradually work in the warm broth and a teaspoon of salt until you have a soft, spreadable dough.
Lightly boil the carrots and peas for a few minutes so they are just tender.
Place a spoonful of dough on a banana leaf square and flatten it. Add a little pork, rice, carrot, peas, a strip of bell pepper and a slice of potato.
Cover with a little more dough, fold the leaf into a neat rectangular parcel and tie with string, usually in pairs.
Lower the tamales into a large pot of boiling water, or steam them over water, for about 1.5 to 2 hours until the dough is firm.
Rest for 10 minutes and unwrap to serve, traditionally with coffee.
